# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My thinking: I'm the Mute — my only channel is gestures, and only the Deaf can see them. The Blind can't receive anything from me directly; everything I know must flow through the Deaf, who can then speak it aloud to the Blind.

What I know from the manual so far: the light cycles through seven colours, and only its colour at the moment of the cut matters. Row one: blue light → cut the yellow wire. The Deaf can see the light and the wires but has no manual; the Blind can cut but neither sees nor knows the rule. So the Deaf is my bridge — but gestures have no meanings yet. Before I can transmit "blue means yellow," somebody has to build a vocabulary with me.

The fastest bootstrap is a binary channel: 👍 and 👎 are almost universally readable as yes/no. I send those now, prefaced by a wave so the Deaf reads it as "I am starting a code," not as an answer. The Deaf sees this in this very round (they come after me), so they can immediately start asking yes/no questions aloud — or, better, read off a numbered list of candidate mappings ("blue→yellow? blue→red? ..."), assign each candidate a gesture, and have me echo the true ones. That gives us real bandwidth: I hold the manual rows, they build the codebook, the Blind gets spoken orders.

Round one is for establishing the link, not for defusing — the Blind can't be reached by me at all this turn, and the Deaf doesn't yet know what to tell them.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎"])
```

You hold the manual: apply it to Deaf's spoken description. Then send me the verdict THROUGH Deaf, because I cannot see your gestures: gesture to Deaf with this code - ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 👌 means cut now, ✊ means do not cut or wait. Deaf will see the gesture and speak it to me. If the manual needs more detail from my hands, gesture your question to Deaf and Deaf can relay it to me aloud. Also tell me if the manual mentions a timer or anything about the display or light - Deaf may need to look for something specific.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb report: the display reads 0. There is a light and it is purple. There are three wires: wire one yellow, wire two red, wire three green. That is everything printed or shown on it. Please look all of this up in the manual. Answer me only with gestures, and use this code from now on: thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. When I number options in my messages, one finger is option one, two fingers option two, the three-finger sign option three. Folded hands means you need more information from me. I will resend these readings every round in case anything changes.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🙏]

My thinking: Piecing the worlds together now. Deaf sees: display 0, light purple, wires yellow/red/green in positions 1/2/3. Blind can cut 1, 2 or 3. My manual so far holds exactly one row: blue light → yellow wire. The light is currently purple — which is not in my table — so there is no safe cut this round. Blind already promised not to cut without an answer, and I must reinforce that.

And I don't actually need to transmit the whole rule in words. The manual says only the light colour *at the moment of the cut* matters, and the light changes every round. So the conditional can live in timing: I wait until Deaf reports the light is blue, and only then send ☝ + 👌 ("wire 1, cut now"). Blue → yellow, and yellow is wire 1.

What Blind asked that I can answer now: manual mentions nothing about the display or a timer (so far), and the current reading — purple light — is not in the table. That's a "no," plus "don't cut" in Blind's own code, plus a request to Deaf to keep the readings coming every round.


My thinking: The light is yellow this round. My manual has exactly one row — blue light → yellow wire — so there is no authorized cut now. The critical thing is to keep everyone's hands still until the light is blue, and I must be careful about how I even say "wait."

I've spotted a lethal inconsistency: Blind privately gave me a code where 👌 means "cut now" and ✊ means "don't cut." Deaf, who never saw that message (it was addressed to me), has now declared his own spoken code where ✊ means "cut" and 👌 means "do nothing" — the exact opposite. Since the only path to Blind runs through Deaf's voice, whatever Deaf says aloud is what governs. So I will not use ✊ or 👌 at all until both of them have explicitly settled on one codebook in speech. Sending either symbol right now risks Deaf voicing the meaning while Blind decodes the symbol, inverting a cut order. Number gestures (☝ ✌ 🤟) and 👍/👎 are safe — they mean the same thing in both books, and Deaf's order format requires number plus verb, so bare numbers can't be misread as orders.

What I actually need this round, in priority order: (1) Deaf and Blind must align their wire numbering out loud — Deaf sees the row of wires, Blind feels positions 1/2/3, and if they count from opposite ends my eventual "wire 1" kills us. (3) The protocol I'm building toward: Deaf reports the light colour aloud every round; I hear it, and only when the reported colour matches a manual row do I gesture that row's wire number; Deaf voices it; Blind cuts in the same round, before the light changes again. That needs no colour vocabulary at all and avoids every contested symbol.

I'm also answering Deaf's question — yes, my rules depend on the light colour — so he knows the light is the variable to watch and announce. I'm deliberately sending no cut or wait verb: Blind has sworn not to cut without an order through Deaf's voice, so "question, no order" is the safe state. The display reading 0 hasn't moved in three rounds; nothing in my manual mentions it so far, and I'll flag that once we have the vocabulary to discuss it.
